Lessons.Title: Writing and Graphing Systems of Linear Equations
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: write two equations for simultaneous constraints, graph both, and interpret their intersection as the pair satisfying the full system. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U02:L12, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/12/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). Building On 8.EE.C.8.a and 8.EE.C.8.b; Addressing HSA-CED.A.3, HSA-REI.A and HSA-REI.C.6; Building Towards HSA-REI.C.6.

Original ticket-sale scenario: a museum sold a total of 20 tickets, adult tickets $8 and child tickets $5. Its reported revenue is $136. Let a be adult tickets and c child tickets. Constraints a+c=20 and 8a+5c=136, with a,c whole and nonnegative. Graph each line on the same labeled axes and identify their shared intersection.

To locate intersection, subtract 5 times the first equation from the second: 3a=36, so a=12 and c=8. Verify 12+8=20 and 8(12)+5(8)=96+40=136. The crossing represents both constraints, not merely one line's allowed points.

Student task: draw both independent original lines, mark the meaningful first-quadrant integer intersection, identify two other pairs that satisfy only one constraint, and explain why a correct system requires all restrictions. Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, max 8): appropriate variable definitions, accurate graphs and shared scale, verified intersection, and interpretation of why off-intersection pairs fail.

KeyConcepts.Title: System
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiple equations constrain the same unknown values simultaneously.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Every equation must be true at a system solution.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph intersection
KeyConcepts.Definition: A common point of two lines solves both equations.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Substitute its coordinates into each equation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Context domain
KeyConcepts.Definition: Counts of sold tickets must be whole and nonnegative.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not accept negative or fractional counts even when lines extend.
KeyConcepts.Example: a=12, c=8 are valid ticket counts.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find simultaneous ticket counts
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve a+c=20, 8a+5c=136.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both total count and revenue match.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check a pair on one line only
WorkedExamples.Question: Is (10,10) a system solution?
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
Steps: The pair lies on the total-tickets line but not on the revenue line.
Therefore it is not the intersection.
WorkedExamples.Answer: No, (10,10) is not a system solution.
WorkedExamples.Check: All equations must be satisfied, not just one.

WorkedExamples.Title: Interpret the axes
WorkedExamples.Question: What do intercepts of a+c=20 mean compared with its valid intersection?
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
Steps: Intercept (20,0) models 20 adults and no children.
Intercept (0,20) models no adults and 20 children.
Neither gives revenue $136: totals are $160 and $100.
The second constraint selects intersection (12,8) from the first line.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Only the shared point (12,8) meets both statements.
WorkedExamples.Check: Check ticket counts and dollar sums.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating any point on either line as a system solution
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The intersection must satisfy both equations.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Graphing without axis units and domains
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A coordinate could be misread or imply impossible quantities.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label adult tickets, child tickets and nonnegative count domain.

SummaryPoints: A system solution satisfies every constraint simultaneously.
The graph intersection visualizes that shared solution.
For the original ticket model, the valid solution is (a,c)=(12,8).
Teacher checks actual graphs and contextual reasoning.
